```{r setup, include=FALSE}

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning=FALSE, message= FALSE)

# 1. Load libraries:

library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)

# 2.  Read in data (as we did in Labs 1 and 2):

listings_clean <- readRDS("listings_clean.rds")

# 3. Check if the variables room_type and property_type are in the appropriate format and that price is restricted to a suitable range:

listings_clean |> select (room_type, property_type) |> glimpse ()

range(listings_clean$price)


```

## Histogram of price:

```{r}

listings_clean |>
  ggplot(aes(price)) +
  geom_histogram(colour="deepskyblue4", fill="deepskyblue3", binwidth=10) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of prices of Airbnb listings in Edinburgh",
       subtitle = "Prices restricted to the range from £25 to £1,000",
       x = "Price (£)",
       y = "Count",
       caption = "Source: InsideAirbnb.com") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1000, by = 200)) +
  theme_minimal()


```


## Density plot of price by room type:
\
The Y-axis represents probability density and is scaled so that the area under the curve equals 1. \

The y-values are probability densities. They tell you how concentrated the data are around different x-values. \

Because the area under the curve = 1, you can interpret areas under parts of the curve as probabilities: \

e.g., the proportion of data between x = £25 and x = £200 equals the area under the curve between £25 and £200. \

If most of the curve’s area lies between £25 and £200, that means most listings_clean fall in that price range. \

For example, if the area under the curve between between £25 and £200 is 0.85, then about 85% of the listings_clean fall within this range. \
 
However, you can't gauge the precise area of the curve that falls between two x values by just looking at the plot.  \

**Generally**: \

Areas under taller, wider parts of the curve represent higher concentrations of data. \

A tall, narrow peak means the data are tightly concentrated (less spread). \

A low, wide curve means more spread. \

```{r}

listings_clean |>
  ggplot(aes(price, fill = room_type)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of prices of Airbnb listings in Edinburgh by room type",
       subtitle = "Prices restricted to a range from £25 to £1,000",
       x = "Price (£)",
       y = "Probability density",
       caption = "Source: InsideAirbnb.com",
       fill = "Room type") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1000, by = 200)) +
  theme_minimal()

```

```{r density-facets, fig.width=12, fig.height=4}

listings_clean |>
  ggplot(aes(price, fill = room_type)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of prices of Airbnb listings in Edinburgh by room type",
    subtitle = "Prices restricted to a range from £25 to £1,000",
    x = "Price (£)",
    y = "Probability density",
    caption = "Source: InsideAirbnb.com",
    fill = "Room type"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1000, by = 200)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  facet_wrap(~ room_type, ncol = 3)


```

## Histogram of review_scores_rating:


```{r}

# A histogram of review_scores_rating: 

listings_clean |>
  drop_na(review_scores_rating) |>
  ggplot(aes(review_scores_rating)) +
  geom_histogram(colour="deepskyblue4", fill="deepskyblue3") +
  expand_limits(x = 0) + # otherwise won't start at zero
  labs(title = "Distribution of average review score of Airbnb listings in Edinburgh",
       x = "Review score (out of 100)",
       y = "Count",
       caption = "Source: InsideAirbnb.com") +
  theme_minimal()

range(listings_clean$review_scores_rating, na.rm=TRUE)

```


## Density plot of review_scores_rating:

```{r}

listings_clean |>
  drop_na(review_scores_rating) |>
  ggplot(aes(review_scores_rating)) +
  geom_density(fill="deepskyblue3") +
  expand_limits(x = 0) + # otherwise won't start at zero
  labs(title = "Distribution of average review score of Airbnb listings_clean in Edinburgh",
       x = "Review score (out of 100)",
       y = "Probability density",
       caption = "Source: InsideAirbnb.com") +
  theme_minimal()

```


## Density plot of review_scores_rating by room_type:

```{r}

listings_clean |>
  drop_na(review_scores_rating) |> #Make sure you exclude the NAs.
  ggplot(aes(review_scores_rating, fill = room_type)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5) +
  expand_limits(x = 0) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of review ratings of Airbnb listings_clean in Edinburgh",
       x = "Review score (out of 100)",
       y = "Probability density",
       caption = "Source: InsideAirbnb.com",
       fill = "Room type") +
  theme_minimal()

```



```{r density-facets2 , fig.width=12, fig.height=4}


listings_clean |>
  drop_na(review_scores_rating) |> #Make sure you exclude the NAs.
  ggplot(aes(review_scores_rating, fill = room_type)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5) +
  expand_limits(x = 0) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of review ratings of Airbnb listings_clean in Edinburgh",
       x = "Review score (out of 100)",
       y = "Probability density",
       caption = "Source: InsideAirbnb.com",
       fill = "Room type") +
  theme_minimal() +
  facet_wrap(~ room_type, ncol = 3)


```
